name: The Heron warehouse
description: A tall, tarred timber warehouse at the downriver end of the wharves, half on the wharf and half on piles over the river, under a painted heron. Inside, one long floor lit by lanterns and thick with grain dust; outside, the dark, the river and a barge waiting for the ebb.

areas.name: the wharf outside the land door
areas.description: The end of the wharf, where the lamps give out: Saul's sentry box and brazier by the land door, Duchess across the threshold, bollards, and the drop to the river.

areas.name: the re-sacking floor
areas.description: One long floor lit by lanterns, the grain dust hanging in the light like fog: the palace's wheat-ear sacks down the north side, heron sacks down the south, the gang slitting, pouring and sewing between them.

areas.name: the counting-box (up a short stair, over the floor)
areas.description: A glass-sided box hung over the floor in the north-east corner: a high desk, a lamp, and the true book under Mister Scrope's hand.

areas.name: the plank walk on the piles
areas.description: Slippery planks on the piles along the river side, round to the low river door; the river runs fast and black underneath.

areas.name: the barge Patience
areas.description: The Saltmere barge Patience, broad and low, moored alongside under the hoist, hatches open, her bargees waiting for the ebb.

things.name: the land door
things.description: Big double doors with a wicket in one leaf, barred inside on loading nights: only the Master comes in this way, at the midnight bell.

things.name: the watchman's sentry box
things.description: A cupboard with ideas above its station, a stool inside and forty years of newspapers.

things.name: the watchman's brazier
things.description: Glowing by the land door, a kettle on it and Duchess's dinner warming beside it.

things.name: Duchess
things.description: A vast, elderly brindle mastiff with a face like a collapsed sofa, asleep across the land door's threshold. She snores, drools and has opinions about smells.

things.name: a bollard at the wharf's edge
the Heron's signboard
things.description: A painted heron on one leg, looking down its beak at the wharf.

things.name: the river door
things.description: A low loading door at water level with a grille in it. The gang hold a brass heron token up to the grille, and whoever's nearest inside draws the bolt.

things.name: the hoist
things.description: Worked from the floor, just inside the river door: a winch and a creaking rope that runs up and out over a pulley on the beam above the door, swinging sacks out and down into the barge. Whoever's on it is in among the gang, in plain view of the counting-box.

things.name: the hoist rope
things.description: Tarred and creaking, hauled hand over hand from the winch, out over the beam's pulley and down into the barge's hold.

things.name: the river
things.description: High, fast, black and cold under the floor, and the tide on the turn.

things.name: the chute
things.description: A wooden chute from the floor down through the river door into the barge's hold. Sacks go down it with a noise like a giant swallowing.

things.name: the palace's wheat-ear sacks
things.description: Stacked to the beams down the north side, every one stamped with the royal wheat-ear: the King's grain, forty sacks still to go.

things.name: the heron sacks
things.description: New sacks stamped with a heron, sewn shut and stacked down the south side, ready for the chute.

things.name: a heap of empty wheat-ear sacks
things.description: Waiting for the river at the end of the night, a stone in each. Evidence, if anyone wanted it.

things.name: the trestles
things.description: Where the gang slit the wheat-ear sacks, pour the grain and sew it up in heron sacks.

things.name: a brazier for cold hands
things.description: Burning merrily in the middle of the grain dust.

things.name: a sign: NO NAKED LIGHTS
things.description: Painted in red. Everyone ignores it, and the brazier is right under it.

things.name: a lantern hung from the beams
a lantern hung from the beams
the re-sacking gang
things.description: Six porters in grain-white with knives and sack-needles, working fast, heads down, not talking.

things.name: the short stair to the counting-box
the clerk's desk
things.description: A high clerk's desk, ink-stained, with a lamp over it.

things.name: the Heron's true book
things.description: A fat ledger bound in green calf with a brass clasp, in Scrope's small careful hand: every 'lost' King's Road wagon by its Granary Roll number, re-sacked under the heron and sold downriver, the Master's share, and 'J.S.' on every page.

things.name: a bag of new heron pennies
things.description: The Master's share for tonight, counted twice.

things.name: the Patience's open hatches
things.description: Her hold half full of heron sacks.

things.name: the bargees
things.description: Saltmere bargees in oilskins, pipes lit, waiting for the ebb and very carefully not asking.

things.name: the Heron's day book
things.description: The book anyone may see, in Scrope's small careful hand: tonight's lot entered as condemned stock, lawfully sold by the Royal Purveyor's office. It proves nothing but the story it tells.

things.name: the Patience's bill of lading
things.description: From the Heron to her master: heron sacks of condemned grain, lawfully sold, for Saltmere. It says what the day book says.

things.name: Hep's tally stick
things.description: In her apron pocket: a notch for every sack she skims a night for the gang's families, in nobody's book but hers.

kell.note: at the player's side on the dark wharf

saul.note: by his brazier at the land door

hep.note: between the stacks, driving the gang

scrope.note: at his desk, his left hand on the true book

hobb.note: on the hoist by the river door, working it one-handed

sallow.note: at the land door with his lantern-boy and the Crakes
